text: Task 3: XML Schema Design
Nov 2, 2026 · @Sakib

Three XSDs define every message the Task 2 services exchange: a shared common-types schema imported by a Payment Instruction schema and a Net Settlement schema. Both sample documents validate against their schemas, and a deliberately malformed instruction is rejected at the API Gateway with four specific errors rather than failing later inside the orchestration.
Schema architecture and reuse

The design uses three schemas rather than two. The types shared between messages — a BIC, a currency, an amount, a status code — are defined once in a common library and imported, so tightening the BIC pattern changes one file instead of being edited separately in every message schema and drifting out of step.

The three root elements of PaymentInstruction.xsd are exactly the three WSDL message parts declared in Task 2, so the service contract and the schema cannot drift apart: the WSDL <types> section imports this file rather than redefining anything.

<!-- PapssCommonTypes.xsd — the reusable types, abridged --><xsd:simpleType name="UETRType">  <xsd:restriction base="xsd:string">    <xsd:pattern value="[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}"/>  </xsd:restriction></xsd:simpleType><xsd:simpleType name="BICType">  <xsd:restriction base="xsd:string">    <xsd:pattern value="[A-Z]{6}[A-Z2-9][A-NP-Z0-9]([A-Z0-9]{3})?"/>  </xsd:restriction></xsd:simpleType><!-- A closed list, not a free ISO 4217 pattern: an unregistered     currency is refused at the gateway, not deep in Pre-Funding Management --><xsd:simpleType name="CurrencyCodeType">  <xsd:restriction base="xsd:string">    <xsd:enumeration value="GHS"/>    <xsd:enumeration value="NGN"/>    <xsd:enumeration value="USD"/>    <xsd:enumeration value="KES"/>    <xsd:enumeration value="ZAR"/>  </xsd:restriction></xsd:simpleType><xsd:simpleType name="AmountValueType">  <xsd:restriction base="xsd:decimal">    <xsd:minInclusive value="0.01"/>    <xsd:totalDigits value="18"/>    <xsd:fractionDigits value="2"/>  </xsd:restriction></xsd:simpleType><!-- Currency travels with the figure, so an amount can never be read     in the wrong currency by a downstream participant --><xsd:complexType name="AmountType">  <xsd:simpleContent>    <xsd:extension base="cmn:AmountValueType">      <xsd:attribute name="Ccy" type="cmn:CurrencyCodeType" use="required"/>    </xsd:extension>  </xsd:simpleContent></xsd:complexType>

Three amount types are defined rather than one, because the three uses have genuinely different valid ranges: AmountType must be at least 0.01, since a payment of nothing is a defect; NonNegativeAmountType allows zero, because a participant can legitimately post no debits in a cycle; and SignedAmountType allows negative values, because a net settlement position is a debit or a credit. Collapsing them into one type would mean the schema could no longer reject a zero-value payment.

Two further decisions apply to all three schemas. elementFormDefault="qualified" makes every element carry its namespace, so a PaymentId in a payment message stays distinguishable from any same-named element in a settlement message as both pass through the shared ESB. A SchemaVersion attribute fixed="1.0" on each root element means a participant still running an older adapter is rejected at the gateway with an explicit version error, instead of silently sending a message the hub parses differently from the way the sender meant it.
Payment Instruction schema
PaymentInstruction.xsd carries the WS-01 request as a group header plus one to one hundred credit transfer transactions, so a single payment and a small batch share one structure.

<xsd:element name="PaymentInstruction" type="pay:PaymentInstructionType">  <!-- A payment may appear only once in a batch -->  <xsd:unique name="UniquePaymentId">    <xsd:selector xpath="pay:CreditTransferTransaction"/>    <xsd:field xpath="pay:PaymentId"/>  </xsd:unique></xsd:element><xsd:complexType name="PaymentInstructionType">  <xsd:sequence>    <xsd:element name="GroupHeader" type="pay:GroupHeaderType"/>    <xsd:element name="CreditTransferTransaction"                 type="pay:CreditTransferTransactionType"                 minOccurs="1" maxOccurs="100"/>  </xsd:sequence>  <xsd:attribute name="SchemaVersion" type="xsd:string"                 use="required" fixed="1.0"/></xsd:complexType><xsd:complexType name="CreditTransferTransactionType">  <xsd:sequence>    <xsd:element name="PaymentId"              type="cmn:UETRType"/>    <xsd:element name="EndToEndId"             type="cmn:ReferenceType"/>    <xsd:element name="InstructedAmount"       type="cmn:AmountType"/>    <xsd:element name="SettlementCurrency"     type="cmn:CurrencyCodeType"/>    <xsd:element name="FxQuoteReference"       type="cmn:ReferenceType" minOccurs="0"/>    <xsd:element name="FxRate"                 type="cmn:FxRateType"    minOccurs="0"/>    <xsd:element name="RequestedExecutionDate" type="xsd:date"/>    <xsd:element name="ChargeBearer"           type="cmn:ChargeBearerType"/>    <xsd:element name="PurposeCode"            type="pay:PurposeCodeType"/>    <xsd:element name="Debtor"                 type="cmn:PartyType"/>    <xsd:element name="DebtorAgent"            type="cmn:AgentType"/>    <xsd:element name="Creditor"               type="cmn:PartyType"/>    <xsd:element name="CreditorAgent"          type="cmn:AgentType"/>    <xsd:element name="RemittanceInformation"  type="pay:RemittanceType" minOccurs="0"/>    <xsd:element name="SponsorId"              type="cmn:BICType"        minOccurs="0"/>  </xsd:sequence></xsd:complexType>
Every constraint is chosen against a failure it prevents, not applied by habit.

text: The same schema defines PaymentAcknowledgement, the payment status message returned by WS-01, and PaymentFault, the fault detail shown in Task 2.

One limitation is worth stating. RejectReasonCode is optional because it should appear only when AcceptanceStatus is RJCT, but XSD 1.0 cannot express a conditional dependency between two sibling elements — that would need an XSD 1.1 xsd:assert, which many enterprise parsers still do not support. The rule is therefore enforced in the Business Rules component rather than in the schema. Stating this matters: a schema that appears to guarantee a rule it cannot enforce is more dangerous than one whose boundary is documented.
Net Settlement schema

NetSettlementInstruction.xsd carries the WS-05 end-of-day multilateral position. Its shape differs from the payment schema in one way that matters: it is a collection rather than a single transaction, so most of its constraints govern occurrence and uniqueness rather than format.

<xsd:element name="NetSettlementInstruction"             type="stl:NetSettlementInstructionType">  <!-- A participant may hold only one position per settlement cycle -->  <xsd:unique name="UniqueParticipant">    <xsd:selector xpath="stl:ParticipantPositions/stl:ParticipantPosition"/>    <xsd:field xpath="stl:ParticipantId"/>  </xsd:unique></xsd:element><xsd:complexType name="ParticipantPositionsType">  <xsd:sequence>    <!-- A netting cycle requires at least two participants -->    <xsd:element name="ParticipantPosition"                 type="stl:ParticipantPositionType"                 minOccurs="2" maxOccurs="unbounded"/>  </xsd:sequence></xsd:complexType><xsd:complexType name="ParticipantPositionType">  <xsd:sequence>    <xsd:element name="ParticipantId"    type="cmn:BICType"/>    <xsd:element name="ParticipantName"  type="cmn:NameType"/>    <xsd:element name="ParticipantRole"  type="stl:ParticipantRoleType"/>    <xsd:element name="SponsorId"        type="cmn:BICType" minOccurs="0"/>    <xsd:element name="GrossDebits"      type="cmn:NonNegativeAmountType"/>    <xsd:element name="GrossCredits"     type="cmn:NonNegativeAmountType"/>    <xsd:element name="NetAmount"        type="cmn:SignedAmountType"/>    <xsd:element name="TransactionCount" type="xsd:nonNegativeInteger"/>  </xsd:sequence></xsd:complexType><!-- Dual control: exactly two authorising officers --><xsd:element name="AuthorisedBy" type="cmn:NameType"             minOccurs="2" maxOccurs="2"/>

One bank appearing twice and being double-counted in the net total
A free-text cycle reference that Audit & Reconciliation cannot match against its ledger

text: As with the payment schema, one rule sits outside what XSD 1.0 can express. TotalNetAmount must equal the sum of every NetAmount and must come to zero for a balanced cycle, but that is arithmetic across repeating elements, which requires XSD 1.1 assertions. Settlement Orchestration performs the check before dispatch, and a failure raises the SettlementMismatch fault specified in Task 2. The schema guarantees that each figure is well formed and that no participant is counted twice; the business layer guarantees that the figures add up.

How XML validation supports the integration

Validation at the API Gateway is the hub's first control. A message that fails its schema never reaches the ESB, so a defect costs a rejection at the boundary rather than a half-completed payment the orchestration has to unwind.
Error detection, demonstrated

A test message was submitted carrying four defects a real adapter could plausibly produce: a truncated BIC, an unregistered currency, an amount with three decimal places, and a creditor record missing its account number.

<cmn:BICFI>ECOCGH</cmn:BICFI>...<pay:InstructedAmount Ccy="GBP">250000.555</pay:InstructedAmount>...<pay:Creditor>  <cmn:Name>Legos Corp</cmn:Name>  <cmn:Country>NG</cmn:Country>   <!-- Account element missing --></pay:Creditor>

:14: element BICFI: [facet 'pattern'] The value 'ECOCGH' is not accepted     by the pattern '[A-Z]{6}[A-Z2-9][A-NP-Z0-9]([A-Z0-9]{3})?'.:24: element InstructedAmount, attribute 'Ccy': [facet 'enumeration']     The value 'GBP' is not an element of the set {'GHS','NGN','USD','KES','ZAR'}.:24: element InstructedAmount: [facet 'fractionDigits'] The value '250000.555'     has more fractional digits than are allowed ('2').:39: element Country: This element is not expected. Expected is ( Account ).PaymentInstruction_Invalid_Sample.xml fails to validate
Each error names the line, the element, the rule broken and the value that broke it — enough for the sending bank's operations team to correct its adapter without raising a support case with PAPSS.
What validation guarantees

Data integrity. Every amount is a decimal of at most two fraction digits carrying a mandatory currency attribute, so a figure cannot reach the clearing ledger with a rounding error or be read in the wrong currency by the receiving bank. The third error above is exactly that case: GHS 250,000.555 is not an amount any RTGS in the region can post.

Consistency. The participants run different core banking systems that produce different date formats, identifier lengths and internal code values. The schema forces all of them into one canonical representation before the ESB sees the message, which is what allows Audit & Reconciliation to compare a Ghanaian record and a Nigerian record against the same settlement cycle without a per-bank translation step.

Interoperability. The XSD is the machine-readable half of the contract. A participant generates its client classes directly from it, so a bank joining PAPSS integrates against a published definition rather than against prose documentation and trial and error. Because both message schemas import the same common types, a new participant inherits the same BIC, currency and amount rules as everyone already connected.

Error detection. The gateway is the earliest point a defect can be caught and the cheapest point to fix it. Had the currency error passed, it would instead have surfaced at Check Funds, where there is no GBP pre-funding account to debit — after the payment had been accepted and the customer told it was in flight.

Compliance reporting. PurposeCode is mandatory and drawn from a closed list, and Debtor and Creditor must each carry a name and a country. Those are precisely the fields sanctions screening in WS-02 and central bank reporting depend on, so the schema makes it impossible to accept a payment that cannot later be reported. Leaving them optional would push the failure into the compliance step, where a missing field means a manual review rather than an automatic rejection.

Auditability. PaymentId is a version-4 UUID unique across its batch and CycleId follows a fixed pattern, so every message carries a key that Audit & Reconciliation can join on across banks, currencies and cycles. The validated XML is itself the audit record: because it declares the schema version it conforms to, a message retrieved from the archive years later can still be parsed and re-checked against the schema that was in force when it was sent — something a free-text or ad-hoc format cannot guarantee.
What validation does not guarantee

A schema proves a message is well formed, not that it is true. The valid sample would still pass validation if the beneficiary account were closed, if Ecobank Ghana held no GHS pre-funding, or if the creditor appeared on a sanctions list. This is why the Task 2 services declare business faults separately from schema faults, and why TotalNetAmount summing to zero is checked in Settlement Orchestration rather than in the XSD. Validation is the first control in the chain, not the only one.
